# Postmortem: 4h checkout-api outage, DB connection pool exhaustion

Names, times and numbers are illustrative placeholders; swap in your real ones.

**Summary.** On 2026-10-01, 14:02–18:07 UTC (4h05m), `checkout-api` failed ~92% of requests. Downstream `fraud-score` slowed from p99 80ms to 30s+. `checkout-api` calls it inside an open DB transaction with no client timeout, so each slow call pinned a DB connection → pool (50/pod) exhausted → every endpoint failed, including ones that never touch `fraud-score`.

**Impact.** ~92% of checkout requests returned 503 or timed out; ~41k failed orders. No data loss or corruption. 312 support tickets.

## Timeline (UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:55 | `fraud-score` deploys model update; p99 latency starts climbing |
| 14:02 | `checkout-api` pools saturate; 503s begin |
| 14:06 | Page fires: `db_pool_wait_time` high. On-call suspects Postgres |
| 14:20 | DB team engaged; Postgres CPU and locks normal, many `idle in transaction` sessions |
| 14:45 | Rolling restart of `checkout-api` → ~3 min recovery, then re-exhaustion |
| 15:10 | Pods scaled 12 → 24 → hit Postgres `max_connections`, errors worsen |
| 15:40 | Scale-up reverted |
| 16:25 | Thread dump: all workers blocked in `FraudClient.score()` holding a connection |
| 16:35 | `fraud-score` team paged; their dashboard is green (slow, not erroring) |
| 17:10 | `fraud-score` rollback started; slow due to queue backlog |
| 17:40 | Hotfix: 2s timeout on fraud call, fail-open |
| 18:07 | Hotfix fully rolled out; error rate at baseline. Resolved |

## Root cause

`fraud-score`'s deploy was the trigger, but the outage was `checkout-api`'s design:

1. HTTP call to `fraud-score` made inside a DB transaction → connection held for the full downstream latency.
2. No timeout on the HTTP client (library default: infinite) → hold time unbounded.
3. One shared pool for all endpoints, no bulkhead → one slow dependency starved everything.

**Why it took 4h:**

- Alert pointed at the DB, not the dependency → ~2h20m on the wrong system.
- Readiness probe doesn't check pool → pods with no usable connections stayed in rotation.
- `fraud-score` alerted on error rate only, not latency → no page on their side.
- Restart "worked" briefly, which reinforced the wrong theory.
- Scale-up multiplied connections and made it worse.

## Remediations

| # | Action | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Timeouts on all outbound HTTP clients (connect 500ms, total 2s); lint rule bans default client | checkout | Done |
| 2 | Move fraud call outside the transaction; audit other network calls made in transactions | checkout | 10-12 |
| 3 | Circuit breaker + fail-open policy on `fraud-score` | checkout | 10-19 |
| 4 | Pool acquire timeout 1s (fail fast, not queue); Postgres `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` 10s | checkout / DB | 10-12 |
| 5 | Latency SLO alert (p99) on `fraud-score` | fraud | 10-12 |
| 6 | Per-dependency latency panel + alert on `checkout-api` dashboard | checkout | 10-19 |
| 7 | Runbook: pool exhaustion → take thread dump first; do not scale up | SRE | 10-12 |
| 8 | Chaos test: inject 30s latency on each dependency in staging, each quarter | SRE | 11-02 |

**What went well.** No data loss; hotfix built and shipped in under 75 min once the cause was known.
